item.title: MacroMark
item.description: Apple Watch voice capture for people whose notes live in Markdown.
item.content:encoded:
MacroMark is voice capture for people whose notes live in Markdown. Tap your Watch complication, speak, lower your wrist, and let MacroMark append the thought to today's note.

MacroMark 1.0 is live on the App Store and free. Version 1.1 is in testing.

Download on the App Store

Say the shape of the note

Verbal macros turn natural speech into structure. Use the built-in Markdown triggers or create your own phrases for the way you actually capture.

You sayIt writes
“Heading Two”##
“Task”- [ ]
“New Journal Entry”## {date} at {time}
“Dropoff”{location} -
“Block ID”^id-{uuid}
“Not”{backspace}

A note before the thought cools

MacroMark is built around the moment when opening a phone would be enough friction to lose the idea. The Watch collects, the phone processes, and your vault receives one clean Markdown entry.

  1. Tap from your watch face. Deep links open instant capture without a hunt through app screens.
  2. Speak, pause, keep going. The custom audio path is designed for long, messy thoughts instead of tiny dictated snippets.
  3. Lower your wrist to save. Recordings are queued durably on the Watch and delivered to iPhone when the connection is ready.
  4. Land in today's file. Processed notes append to a dated, plain-text daily note in your own files on iCloud Drive — where your Markdown vault already lives — instead of scattering across throwaway documents.

Built for trust

  • Reliability core: Watch captures stay queued until the iPhone has processed them and the export has succeeded or is safely queued for retry.
  • Status and recovery: Export status labels, a needs-attention filter, partial-transcription warnings and retry actions keep capture state visible.
  • Review by date: Check today's, yesterday's or any earlier daily note from the phone inbox or the Watch daily log.
  • App Intents: Instant capture, typed capture, daily-log review and append-text actions are available in Shortcuts and Siri.
  • Setup proof: Settings show where notes go and can write a test note before you rely on Watch capture.
  • Daily-note shape: Timestamp style, separators and an optional append heading are yours to configure.

Privacy stays plain

MacroMark is built around local capture, Apple speech services where applicable, and user-owned note files that stay useful outside the app. It is not a social inbox or analytics product.

Download on the App Store

item.title: NS Marks The Spot
item.description: A source-linked Nova Scotia parcel and tax-sale map, with Fletcher's 1880s sheets as an optional overlay.
item.content:encoded:
NS Marks The Spot is a Nova Scotia map for property research and local history. Search a parcel by PID, civic address, or postal community, read dated municipal tax-sale notices against live parcel geometry, switch on provincial reference layers, and slide Hugh Fletcher's 1880s geological sheets over today's landscape.

Open Online Map

On this pageTime travelFeaturesRhodena WindFishingStatus

Every slider pull is a little time travel

Fade between the old survey and the current map to trace where a road bent, where a shoreline shifted, or where a name survived. The old sheets mark what today's maps forgot — gold mines, foundries, schools — sitting close to where they used to be under the modern roads and woods.

Twenty-four Fletcher sheets, independently georeferenced from David Rumsey Map Collection scans, sit as an optional overlay with an opacity control. A sheet can sit a few hundred metres off modern ground, and the layer says so; it is context, not evidence.

What the map does

  • Parcel search: Enter an eight-digit PID or a Nova Scotia civic address, or tap a visible parcel, and open its provincial boundary in context. Boundaries are approximate context, never a legal survey.
  • Postal communities: Search also recognizes postal communities; a postal candidate becomes selectable only when it resolves to one live provincial civic point.
  • Mailing addresses: When matched, the parcel inspector can show a separately labelled mailing address from Statistics Canada's free National Address Register (June 2026), distinct from the provincial civic address.
  • Tax-sale notices: Municipal tax-sale listings are catalogued as dated snapshots, each pinned to its notice and source document, and mapped against live parcel geometry. No owner names are shown. The Nova Scotia Tax Sale Hub keeps the posted dates in one place.
  • Reference layers: Provincial aerial imagery, property boundaries, Crown land, flood-risk areas, water, roads, contours, geology and mineral records, well-water screening zones, and municipal zoning where a municipality publishes it — each with its own source, licence gate, and attribution.
  • Live location: Optional live location draws the position this device reports on the same map, and the reading stays in that browser.
  • Your maps: Import a GeoPDF, GeoTIFF, shapefile, or GeoJSON and keep it on your device. Nothing is uploaded.
  • Exports: Print a PDF map or export a source-linked evidence note for a parcel.

Rhodena Wind

The proposed turbine map has its own address, /rhodena: the research map with a Rhodena focus, opening as Rhodena Wind — proposed turbine map. The full map stays at /apps/nsmarksthespot/map/.

  • Sight lines: From a chosen viewpoint on the viewshed, an eye-level (~1.7 m) line runs to each assessed 200 m tip in the viewshed colours. It stays solid until bare earth first obstructs it, then a ridge mark and a dotted remainder.
  • Model limits: Those breaks use the same terrain samples, curvature, and refraction as the viewshed. Trees, buildings, and the final design are not in the model; the line is drawn to tip height, not the hub.
  • Edge cases: Near-threshold results stay amber. Unassessed or out-of-range turbines get no line. The layout is the provisional proposed layout.
  • Map | Aerial: A switch under the 3D control. Aerial imagery still opens the Province licence gate before it turns on.

Fishing

The fishing map has its own address, /fishmap: the research map with a fishing focus, opening as Fishing spots — Cape Breton and the Strait of Canso. It is separate from the static Strait and Bras d'Or Fishing Map, and its footer links there.

  • Spots: Numbered pins and spot cards for 27 hand-picked shore, wharf and lake spots, each with its sources and directions in Google Maps or Apple Maps.
  • When and what: Month and species filters and a species calendar. A dated summary of the rules to check hides each rule once its date has passed; the page never says a season is open now. Check the current Anglers' Handbook and DFO notices before you go.
  • Open-data layers: Province stocked-waters records and DFO small craft harbours, alongside the curated spots. A harbour point is not permission to fish from the wharf.

Where it stands

The current product focus is the browser map. It runs on any phone, tablet, or desktop with nothing to install. The native iPhone app is a separate offline and field companion in internal TestFlight builds; it is not on the App Store.

The code is public on GitHub under the MIT licence, structured around a map-engine boundary so the interface can stay steady while the renderer evolves. Map imagery keeps its own licences and attribution, layer by layer. Read more on the project site or in the source on GitHub.

Open Online Map | Rhodena Wind | Fishing | Get help

item.title: Turn Timer
item.description: Visual rounds for real-world countdowns, turns, routines, and reusable sequences.
item.content:encoded:
Turn Timer is a colourful visual countdown you can read from across the room. Start a quick timer, or build a sequence of named rounds for game night, a recipe, a classroom, a meeting or a morning routine, and reuse it whenever you need it.

The browser version runs on any device, with nothing to install, and can be added to your home screen. The iPhone app is a TestFlight beta, not on the App Store yet.

Try it in your browserJoin the iPhone beta

How it works

  1. Start simply. Use the quick timer, or pick an editable starter: Game Night, Recipe Steps, Plant Watering, Classroom Stations, Meeting Agenda or Morning Routine.
  2. Build your sequence. Give each round a name, duration, colour, sound and emoji. Repeat a sequence, pause, skip, restart, or do a turn over.
  3. Keep what you reuse. Save templates, return to recent sessions, and share portable .turntimer files that import without overwriting your own.

Free, with a one-time Pro unlock

Free

  • The quick timer
  • The six starters
  • Playback
  • One custom template
  • Five recent sessions

Turn Timer Pro One-time purchase

  • Unlimited templates
  • Full history and export
  • Sharing
  • Private iCloud sync
  • Template widgets

No subscription, ads or third-party tracking.

item.title: Echo: Audiobook Study Player
item.description: An audiobook player built for studying, not just listening.
item.content:encoded:
Echo is the audiobook player that helps you remember what you heard — word-perfect read-along, one-tap flashcards, and a study system built on the real science of memory.

Why Echo exists

A lot of real listening happens in stolen, interrupted minutes: in and out of the car, an aux cable, an Apple Watch, a chapter cut short. No app on the internet would loop a single chapter until it stuck, stay ready to play on a watch after a long pause, or remember why a bookmark was made three stops ago.

So I built one — an app for iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and Mac that treats audiobooks the way students treat textbooks.

Just here to listen?

You don't have to make a single flashcard. Echo is a full-featured, own-your-library audiobook player first — the study tools are there if you ever want them, and out of the way if you don't.

  • Your books, your device: Import your DRM-free M4B and MP3 files — single books or whole folders. Echo stores its library records and progress on your device. The current release does not expose public-alignment uploads. When network access is permitted, importing a book may look up matching public alignment anchors, with local fallback for an ordinary lookup failure. See the Echo Privacy Policy.
  • Everywhere Apple audio goes: A Watch remote you design, Watch complications, Lock Screen and Control Center playback controls, and Siri bookmarks.
  • The essentials, done right: A sleep timer that fades out or stops at the chapter end, pitch-corrected speed, instant chapter navigation, bookmarks, and background audio tuned for spoken word.
  • Picks up where your attention left off: Adaptive Smart Rewind backs up just enough after a break; pull your headphones and Echo pauses instead of blasting the speaker.
  • Make listening yours: Lay out every transport button, retint the player to your cover art, layer in focus soundscapes, or boost quiet narration past the system max.

Read-along is where most apps stop

A growing crowd of apps will sync your audiobook to your ebook, on your device. That's the floor — Echo does it too. The difference is the two steps above it, where a book actually sticks.

  • Chapter sync — table stakes: Match your audiobook to your ebook chapter by chapter, so you can switch between reading and listening.
  • Word-perfect read-along: Echo follows the narrator word by word — true karaoke, tuned on-device to the real audio, not just snapped to the nearest chapter.
  • Turn it into memory: One tap turns any passage into a spaced-repetition flashcard with its audio snippet attached, and Echo brings it back on your iPhone, Watch, and Mac until you own it.

Sync gets you to the page. Echo gets it into your head.

What Echo does

Echo is in open development toward 1.0. Anything marked 🚧 Coming in 1.0 is being built right now; 🔭 Roadmap means planned after 1.0. Everything else is in the current TestFlight beta.

  • Smart Rewind: Hit play and Echo has already rewound — a little after a short pause, more after hours. Interruptions stop costing you context.
  • Chapter Looping: Repeat one chapter until you own it — the feature Echo was born for. Or loop the exact passage between two bookmarks.
  • Photo Bookmarks: Attach a photo of where you are; the player artwork switches to your photo as you pass that moment again. Your brain files where alongside what — Echo turns that into a memory tool.
  • Voice Memo Bookmarks: Hold a button, speak your thought. Memos play back inline when the narration reaches them.
  • Built-in Spaced Repetition: An Anki-style flashcard system with FSRS / FSRS-4.5 scheduling (the modern Anki scheduler), the narrator's audio on the cards, daily review, and hands-free review on Apple Watch.
  • Mark Now, Card Later: One tap (phone or watch) marks a passage without stopping the narration; the Card Inbox turns marks into flashcards when you have the bandwidth — not mid-sentence.
  • Decks, Tags & Anki Import 🚧 Coming in 1.0: Organize cards into decks, edit any card, review per deck — and import real .apkg Anki decks, scheduling history included.
  • Brain Dump 🚧 Coming in 1.0: A thought hits mid-chapter? Park it — text or voice, even dictated from the watch — without pausing the book. Promote keepers to bookmarks or flashcards later.
  • Context Memory 🚧 Coming in 1.0: Opt in to capture place context with bookmarks, sessions and chapter starts. With permission, the device may supply a precise fix; Echo rounds coordinates before asking Apple's geocoder for a place name and stores the rounded context locally. Local deletion does not erase providers' records or device backups. See the Echo Privacy Policy.
  • Insights That Are Real: Listening time, streaks, chapter coverage ("Ch 7 — 86%, heard 3×"), retention curves, review forecasts — honest numbers from your actual listening, never from a server.
  • Synced EPUB Reader: The text scrolls with the narration, tap a paragraph to jump the audio, search the book and leap to the spoken moment.
  • PDF Companions: Diagrams and page-level material can sit beside the audio, so visual context appears when the narration needs it.
  • On-Device Auto-Alignment: Echo's speech recognition (WhisperKit + CoreML) aligns text to audio in tiers — chapter snap, drift detection, word-level repair. Entirely on your device.
  • Second-Brain Export: One tap exports a book's bookmarks, notes, voice memos, photos, and flashcards as a clean Markdown bundle — straight into Obsidian, Logseq, or Notion. No account, no lock-in.
  • Files, iCloud and Watch: Files in an iCloud folder follow Apple's file services. Watch features transfer selected state and voice memos with the paired iPhone. This release does not promise complete private synchronization of flashcards, decks, bookmarks or playback position. See the Echo Privacy Policy.
  • A Watch Remote You Design: Up to 25 buttons across 5 pages, Digital Crown scrubbing or volume, plus a Pomodoro focus timer on your wrist.
  • Focus Soundscapes & Visualizer: Layer generative white/brown noise, binaural beats, and nature sounds under your narration — and watch four GPU-powered audio visualizers respond as you listen.
  • Pitch-Corrected Speed: Narrators sound human at 1.25×. Every book remembers its own speed.
  • Dyslexia-Friendly by Design: Lexend and OpenDyslexic fonts built in, Dynamic Type, VoiceOver labels.
  • On-Device AI Narration: Generate natural narration for text-only EPUBs entirely on your device — no cloud, no API calls — so books that were never recorded can still be heard.
  • Chapter Study Mode 🔭 Roadmap: Treat chapters like flashcards — listen, grade yourself, and your due chapters become today's listening queue.

One library, four screens

  • Radically private: Core playback and reading need no Echo account. Optional connected services have separate data handling. External AI sends book text to the provider you configure, under that provider's retention and training policies. Read the Echo privacy policy.
  • Open source: Echo is open source under the GPL-3.0 license.
  • No locked files: Echo is built around DRM-free files you own and can see.
  • For Every Mind: Designed for interrupted, neurodivergent attention first — and useful for everyone whose listening gets interrupted.
  • Echo Pro is a one-time unlock: Optional power features, paid once. No subscription.

Learn more

  • Join the TestFlight beta — public beta, also listed on /testflight/
  • Getting the Most Out of Echo — every feature plus the memory science behind it
  • The Focus Field Guide — ADHD & AuDHD strategies: getting started, time blindness, organization, motivation, hyperfocus
  • User Manual — the complete reference for every platform, including library organization
  • Join the Beta — TestFlight guide and test plans
  • Building Echo: The Devlog — how it was built, week by week
  • Help & Support — FAQs and contact

View Source Code on GitHub | Docs | Get Help & Support

item.title: Five apps and a services page
item.description: Where five apps stood in July 2026, and a new services page.
item.content:encoded:
Five apps and a services page

Update, October 2026: MacroMark 1.0 is now on the App Store, free. Routey has been discontinued. See Apps for where each app stands today.

First real post, so a status note rather than a manifesto.

KinNoKi Labs is one person — me, Dan — building Apple-platform apps in Cape Breton, Nova Scotia. Five apps are in the works right now, at different stages:

  • Echo, an audiobook study player
  • MacroMark, Apple Watch voice capture for Markdown notes
  • NS Marks The Spot, historical Nova Scotia maps
  • Turn Timer, a visual sequence timer
  • Routey, an offline-first route organizer (since discontinued)

Four of them have TestFlight builds running; MacroMark is still pre-TestFlight, in development toward V1.0. None are on the App Store yet — getting them there, with the review prep, metadata, and polish that takes, is the current work.

The other new thing is a services page. Building these apps meant building systems around my own repeated work first: checklists, document cleanup, release pipelines, and knowledge bases that remember what I already figured out. Small businesses drown in the same kind of repeated paperwork, so I've written up how I approach that work for other people's workflows.

If any of that is useful to you, or you just want to compare notes: hello@kinnokilabs.com.
